clue.text: Denry Machin as a boy, sure of a trick ?

parts.note: Master is the courtesy title for a boy, as in Master Smith
Denry Machin is the hero of Arnold Bennett's novel The Card, the card of its title

explanation.surface: A literary hero, in his schooldays, is a confident card player.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold Bennett's novel The Card follows Denry Machin, a 'card' (a cheeky, clever fellow), so the boy version is Master Card; in bridge or whist a master card is the highest left in a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In card play the master card is the highest remaining in its suit, so it is certain to win the trick.

clue.text: Vermin follow the civil engineer

explanation.surface: Rodents trail after a bridge builder.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters M.I.C.E. stand for Member of the Institution of Civil Engineers, and so follow such an engineer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mice are small rodent pests, and the initials for membership of the engineers' institution come after the holder's name.

clue.text: Whereon" the present hour was ever marked with shade"

definitions.text: Whereon" the present hour was ever marked with shade"

parts.words: Whereon" the present hour was ever marked with shade"
parts.note: a line of verse describing an instrument on which a shadow shows the hour

explanation.surface: A quotation from a poem about telling the time by shadow.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'mark'd'. The shade is the shadow cast by the gnomon, which falls on the dial to show the present hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden timepiece shows the hour by the shadow its pointer casts across a marked face.

clue.text: It was late for recruiting vineyard workers

definitions.text: It was late for recruiting vineyard workers

parts.words: It was late for recruiting vineyard workers
parts.note: in the Gospel parable of the labourers, the master hires the last workers late in the day and pays them the same

explanation.surface: A remark that a farmer left it late to hire grape pickers.
explanation.walkthrough: In Matthew 20 the householder hires labourers at intervals through the day, the last at the eleventh hour, which is where the phrase for the last possible moment comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase meaning the latest possible moment comes from the Gospel parable in which the final labourers are hired an hour before sunset.

clue.text: Was this cat told to " say cheese *' ?

definitions.text: Was this cat told to " say cheese *' ?

parts.words: Was this cat told to " say cheese *' ?
parts.note: photographers say cheese to make people smile, and this cat from Alice in Wonderland is famous for its grin

explanation.surface: A question whether a cat was asked to smile for a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's Cheshire Cat grins constantly; the clue asks whether it got that way by being told to smile for the camera, and Cheshire is also famous for a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheshire Cat in Alice in Wonderland is known for its broad grin, and the English county also gives its name to a cheese.

clue.text: Paladin as a match for a Cromwell?

explanation.surface: A knight of Charlemagne is set against the Lord Protector.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'a Roland for an Oliver' means a blow for a blow, an equal match; Oliver is Cromwell's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Roland was the most famous of Charlemagne's twelve knights, and the old idiom pairs him with his equal Oliver.

clue.text: Abbreviated tree-lined routes for the birds?

explanation.surface: Shortened avenues are laid out for birdwatchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ave is the short form of avenue, a street lined with trees, and Aves is the zoological class containing all birds.

clue.text: Sell 'ouse a place in Paris

parts.note: to vend is to sell
a house is a home, and with the h dropped as in 'ouse it becomes 'ome

explanation.surface: A Cockney sells his house and moves to a spot in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''ouse' says the h is dropped, so the synonym HOME also loses its h.
explanation.definitionFit: The Place Vendome is a famous square in central Paris.

clue.text: How impressively the 11 sounded in 9' sears!

definitions.text: How impressively the 11 sounded in 9' sears

parts.words: How impressively the 11 sounded in 9' sears
parts.note: the clock struck midnight, the time in 11 down, and that chiming was what the fairy-tale heroine at 9 across heard

explanation.surface: An exclamation at how loud a clock's chimes seemed to a listener.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is WITCHING HOUR and '9' is CINDERELLA: the clock striking twelve forced her to flee, and the adverb means both impressively and in the manner of a clock striking.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in a remarkable way, and also suggests the clock striking the hours that sent the heroine running.

clue.text: Her late-night pass expired at 11

parts.note: the fairy-tale heroine was allowed at the ball only until midnight, the time named in 11 down

explanation.surface: A woman's permission to stay out ran out at a set hour.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is a cross-reference to 11 down, WITCHING HOUR, i.e. midnight, not eleven o'clock; the 'pass' is the fairy godmother's magic, which ended at the stroke of twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: In the pantomime story the fairy godmother's spell lasted only until midnight, when the girl had to flee the prince's ball.

clue.text: Take this ball and spell a N country game

definitions.text: Take this ball and spell a N country game

parts.words: Take this ball and spell a N country game
parts.note: ... and spell is an old game from the north of England, the spell being the trap that flicks up the small ball

explanation.surface: An instruction to pick up a ball and write out the name of a northern game.
explanation.walkthrough: Knur and spell is a traditional Yorkshire and Lancashire game: a small wooden or pottery ball is released from a spring trap (the spell) and struck as far as possible. 'Spell' looks like a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: The small hard ball used in the northern English game of knur and spell is called a knur.

clue.text: Time for the " secret, black and midnight hags "

definitions.text: Time for the " secret, black and midnight hags "

parts.words: Time for the " secret, black and midnight hags "
parts.note: Macbeth greets the three witches with these words, so the time meant is the hour when witches are abroad

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare quotation about the witches in Macbeth, given a time slot.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth addresses the witches as 'you secret, black, and midnight hags' (Act 4, Scene 1).
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight is traditionally the hour when witches and spirits are active, as the quoted crones are.

clue.text: Father-figure's no good as a waiter

explanation.surface: A paternal figure turns out to be poor at serving tables.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says 'time and tide wait for no man', so time is no good at waiting; 'Father-figure' is Father Time.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Time is the bearded figure with a scythe who personifies passing years, and the proverb says it waits for nobody.

clue.text: Crafty product of a palmist's job ?

explanation.surface: Something made by a craftsman is compared to a fortune-teller's trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as 'hand' work: a palm reader works on hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Handiwork is something made by skill with the hands, and a palmist reads palms, so the job is literally work on hands.

clue.text: A silly fellow about scene-changing, this teenager

indicators.note: about means going round, so the dim person's letters surround the rearranged word

parts.note: a dolt is a stupid person

indicators.note: changing says the letters of scene are altered in order

explanation.surface: A foolish chap fusses about a stage set, as a teenager would.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'scene-changing' hides that 'changing' is the anagram signal working on scene; 'this teenager' is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a young person in the years between childhood and adulthood.

clue.text: Told airy fabrication, delaying matters

indicators.note: a fabrication is something made up, so the letters of the two words are made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone told a far-fetched lie and kept putting things off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabrication' looks like a noun for a lie but rearranges TOLD AIRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory means tending to put things off or cause delay, so it describes delaying matters.

clue.text: Riddle to help the batsman see the bowler

definitions.text: to help the batsman see the bowler

explanation.surface: A puzzle is set in a cricket match, apparently to aid the man at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' is not a puzzle but a coarse sieve. In cricket, a sight screen is a large white board behind the bowler so the batsman can see the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a coarse sieve, as is a screen for grading gravel, and cricket's sight screen sits behind the bowler to give a clear background.

clue.text: Babbling of a London borough

explanation.surface: Someone is talking nonsense about part of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Havering is an outer London borough in the east of the city; to haver is northern and Scottish for to talk nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To haver is to talk foolishly, and Havering is a borough in east London.

clue.text: What one does best last

parts.note: the proverb says he who ... last ... best, so this is the action done best by the one who does it last

explanation.surface: A comment on which activity is best saved until the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'he who laughs last laughs best' reverses here into a description of the action.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying holds that the person who gets the final chuckle enjoys it most, so the third person verb is what one does best last.

clue.text: Things most beautiful are most ----- said Ruskin

definitions.text: Things most beautiful are most ----- said Ruskin

parts.words: Things most beautiful are most ----- said Ruskin
parts.note: John Ruskin wrote that the most beautiful things are the least practical, peacocks and lilies for instance

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from a Victorian art critic.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruskin, in The Stones of Venice: 'Remember that the most beautiful things in the world are the most useless; peacocks and lilies for instance.'
explanation.definitionFit: Ruskin's point is that beauty serves no practical purpose, so the beautiful things are of no use.

clue.text: But not too much of a bad thing for young oliver

definitions.text: But not too much of a bad thing for young oliver

parts.words: But not too much of a bad thing for young oliver
parts.note: Oliver Twist famously asked for more gruel, while the phrase a bit of a bowlful means too much of something unpleasant

explanation.surface: A remark that an orphan in a Dickens novel could never have too much.
explanation.walkthrough: British slang 'a bit of a basinful' means more than enough of something bad; Oliver Twist, starved in the workhouse, held out his bowl and asked for more, so for him it was never too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl filled to the brim of gruel was exactly what the hungry Dickens orphan wanted, though the idiom treats a full bowl as an excess of trouble.

clue.text: Made a pretence of feeding, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word might be some other arrangement of the same letters

explanation.surface: Someone only pretended to be eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges FEEDING.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign is to pretend, so the past tense describes a pretence made.

clue.text: Father poet up on a high plain in S America

definitions.text: a high plain in S America

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Omar Khayyam is the Persian poet of the Rubaiyat

explanation.surface: Dad and a poet climb onto an Andean plateau.
explanation.walkthrough: Omar Khayyam, author of the Rubaiyat, is a crossword favourite for 'poet'; 'on' simply places the reversed poet after Father in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramo is a high, treeless plateau in the tropical Andes.

clue.text: Shuffle, please cut, and chance your luck

indicators.note: shuffling mixes cards up, so the letters of the words that follow are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A card player asks you to shuffle, cut the pack and take a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shuffle' sits naturally in the card-game picture, but it rearranges PLEASE CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To speculate is to take a risk on an uncertain outcome hoping for gain, which is gambling on your luck.

clue.text: All that remained of a 4 cat

definitions.text: All that remained of a 4 cat

parts.words: All that remained of a 4 cat
parts.note: in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland the cat named in 4 down fades away until only its smile is left

explanation.surface: Only a trace of a particular feline was left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' cross-refers to 4 down, CHESHIRE; the Cheshire Cat in Alice in Wonderland vanishes leaving its smile hanging in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's cat disappears slowly, its broad smile being the last part to go.

clue.text: A bun for this do ?

parts.note: a bun is a style of putting tresses up, and a do is short for a ...

explanation.surface: A question whether a bread roll will be served at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bun' looks like a cake and 'do' a party; together they are a hairstyle and a hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A bun is a way of coiling the tresses on your head, so it is a style or do for them.

clue.text: Not an odd part of 3

indicators.note: part of says the letters lie inside the entry named by the number that follows

parts.note: 3 refers to the entry at 3 down

explanation.surface: Something that is not uneven makes up a piece of another number.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' is the answer to 3 down, ELEVENTH HOUR, and the letters sit inside its first word: el-EVEN-th.
explanation.definitionFit: An even number is one divisible by two, the opposite of an odd one.

clue.text: African oil order replaced in the US

indicators.note: when the order of letters is replaced, the two words are rearranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: An African oil company is reorganised within America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order replaced' rearranges AFRICAN OIL; the definition is loose, the answer being simply a place in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: California is a state on the Pacific coast of the United States.

clue.text: It's nonsense to call for quiet

parts.note: sh is the sound made to ask for silence

explanation.surface: Someone declares that demanding silence is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is informal British slang for rubbish or foolish talk.

clue.text: Crude adjunct of a horse breaker

parts.note: crude means rough, unrefined
a rider is an addition attached to a document or statement

explanation.surface: A coarse accessory belonging to a man who tames horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjunct' means an addition, as a rider is a clause added to a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough-rider is someone who breaks in untrained horses.
